newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Higher oil costs kick up South African Dec PPI.
newsitem.headline: Higher oil costs kick up South African Dec PPI.

text.p: A sharp increase in the cost of crude petroleum imports contributed to a jump in South African producer price inflation in December, the Central Statistical Service said on Thursday.

The annual rate of increase in the overall producer price index in December rose to 8.8 percent from 8.5 percent in November, the highest level since July 1995, although it was only marginally ahead of expectations of 8.7 percent.

Month-on-month, the all commodities index rose 1.0 percent in December from November, but the imported products component rose 1.8 percent, largely reflecting a 9.5 percent increase in the price of crude oil.
In November the imported price of crude showed a monthly decline of 6.6 percent, a fall which the CSS put down the arrival of several large consignments at good prices.
Economists have in recent months questioned the reliability of the imported oil component in the PPI data which has fluctuated widely.
